title: Trinity Sunday
hook: the one Sunday for the mystery at the heart of it all

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pentecost in red: wind, fire, and a crowd hearing the news in the languages they were born with. Your line was every tongue. Whose thank you did you learn? Day one thousand forty-two.

There's a legend told about Augustine, the North African bishop and writer. He's walking along a beach, turning a hard question over and over: how can God be one, and also three? He comes across a child who has dug a little hole in the sand and is running back and forth to the sea with a shell, pouring water into the hole. Augustine asks what he's doing. Putting the sea in this hole, says the child. Augustine laughs: that's impossible. And the child answers, more or less, so is fitting God into your head. Nobody needs the legend to be true for it to land. After the run of Easter and Pentecost, the church calendar keeps one Sunday just for that question. Today, Trinity Sunday.
screen: `THE SEA IN A HOLE IN THE SAND.`

segments.voice: Start with one God. Moses says it in Deuteronomy, in the King James Bible: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD." Jesus quotes it himself when he's asked which commandment comes first. Christians hold on to that line. And yet the Gospels keep naming three together. At Jesus's baptism, in Matthew, the Spirit comes down like a dove, and a voice from heaven says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Father speaking, Son in the water, Spirit descending, all in one scene. At the very end of Matthew, Jesus sends his friends out "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." Some Christian readers point out that it says the name, not the names. And Paul signs off a letter: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all." Over time the church found a word for what these texts hold together: Trinity. One God, Christians who hold the creeds say, in three persons. Not three gods. Not one God wearing three masks. Father, Son and Spirit, each fully God, and one. Then comes a caution. Some teachers in the tradition say that every picture for this falls short. Shamrocks, water and ice and steam: they help a little, and then they leak. That's why Christians call it a mystery. In Christian use, a mystery isn't a puzzle waiting for a clever answer. It's something held to be true that you can live inside without ever getting to the bottom of. The sea doesn't fit in the hole. People still swim in it.
screen: `THE LORD OUR GOD IS ONE LORD.`
`FATHER, SON AND SPIRIT IN ONE SCENE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with a mystery. Settle, and breathe. Don't try to solve anything. Bring to mind something you know is true but can't fully explain. The way a parent loves three children completely. Why a piece of music can bring someone to tears. What a person is, really, behind the face. Stay with it, without explaining it. If you pray, you can rest in Paul's farewell: the grace of Christ, the love of God, the communion of the Spirit. If you don't, simply let the big thing stay big, and sit beside it. The bell holds the time.
Trinity Sunday. The Sunday after Pentecost, kept for the Christian belief in one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit: in Christian words, a mystery to live inside, not a puzzle to solve.
Your line: three in one. Today, when you meet something you can't explain, resist tidying it up, and let it stay a little bigger than you. Day one thousand forty-two.

howItsDone: On Trinity Sunday some churches sing hymns to the Trinity and say a creed, and preachers often take up the texts where Father, Son and Spirit are named together.

what a scholar hears: Deuteronomy's one LORD held alongside texts that name three together, "in the name," singular, of Father, Son and Spirit.

notes: The Augustine and the child on the beach story is presented as 'a legend told about Augustine'; confirm framing.
'Teachers in the tradition say that every picture for this falls short' is a general claim; soften to 'some teachers' if a Keeper prefers.

Trinitarian summary (one God in three persons; not three gods, not one God in three masks) is attributed to 'Christians who hold the creeds'; confirm it is fair and that non-Trinitarian groups are neither named nor judged.
'Over time the church found a word' avoids any date for the term 'Trinity'.
Original left null: τριάς is a church term, not a biblical word, so no original-language word is taught.

Editor pass: dropped 'great' before Augustine (superlative); 'teachers in the tradition say' softened to 'some teachers'; the mystery lines now attribute the belief ('Christians call it', 'held to be true') instead of the narrator asserting it, in the teach, the word and the myth reveal; 'a piece of music undoes you' no longer tells the listener what they feel.

Audit pass: 'notice it says the name, not the names' had the narrator making a doctrinal argument; it is now attributed to 'some Christian readers'. 'Start where the Bible starts' (the Bible starts with Genesis, not Deuteronomy) became 'start with one God'.
